text:
A 1,000Wh power station typically needs **about 250–350 W of solar** to recharge in one day of ordinary sun. The exact figure depends on your peak sun hours and how much of the panel's rating you expect to reach.

**Rule of thumb:** Panel watts ≈ battery Wh ÷ (peak sun hours × ~0.7–0.75)

| Peak sun hours | Panel needed for a one-day recharge |
|---|---|
| 3 | ~450 W |
| 4 | ~335–350 W |
| 4.5 | ~300–320 W |
| 5 | ~270–300 W |
| 6 | ~230–240 W |

The sources use slightly different loss factors, so their numbers vary a bit. Power Preflight's shortcut is to divide the battery's Wh by five, which gives 200 W and about a day and a half of sun ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)). Watt48 gives a 200 W panel about 630 Wh per day at 4.5 peak sun hours, which refills a 1,000 Wh station in a little over a day and a half ([Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station)).

**Other factors:**
- **Winter:** In northern winter, 2 peak sun hours means roughly 700 W or more for a one-day recharge ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).
- **Input cap:** Your station's maximum solar input may be lower than the panel wattage you buy. Extra panel capacity beyond that cap adds nothing on a sunny day, though it helps in weaker light ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge)).
- **Voltage:** Check that the panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) falls within your station's input window. Exceeding it can damage the charge controller ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).

**Example panel:** The ALLPOWERS SP037 is a 400 W foldable panel with a 45.3 V open-circuit voltage, which suits many 12–60 V station inputs. It's listed at $299 at the time of the source's check (October 21, 2026), and the price may have changed ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel)). The page's buy link is an affiliate link, so the site earns a commission if you purchase. Confirm the price and the voltage range against your station's spec sheet before buying.
